questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Jeremiah to purchase?
questions.a: He told Jeremiah to go and purchase a clay jar from someone who makes pottery.

questions.q: Where did Yahweh tell Jeremiah to go?
questions.a: Yahweh told him to go to the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, near the entrance of the Potsherd Gate.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Jeremiah he would bring on the kings of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh said he would bring a disaster on that place that would shock everyone who heard about it.

questions.q: Why is God bringing disaster on Jerusalem?
questions.a: He is bringing disaster because the people have abandoned God and profaned his place and approached other gods and filled the place with innocent blood.

questions.q: Why did the people build shrines to Baal?
questions.a: They built shrines to Baal in order to burn their sons in the fire as burnt offerings to him.

questions.q: What will the Valley of the Son of Hinnom be called?
questions.a: It will be called the Valley of Slaughter.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say would happen to the dead bodies of the people of Judah and Jerusalem?
questions.a: Yahweh said the birds and wild animals would eat their dead bodies.

questions.q: What will everyone who passes by the city do?
questions.a: They will be horrified and will gasp because of all its destruction.

questions.q: What will the people do because of hunger during the siege?
questions.a: They will eat the flesh of their own sons and daughters, and each person will eat the flesh of his neighbor.

questions.q: What was Jeremiah to do with the clay jar?
questions.a: He was to break the jar in front of the men who went with him.

questions.q: What did Yahweh compare breaking the people and the city to?
questions.a: Yahweh compared it to breaking a potter’s jar that can never be put back together.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say the city would become like?
questions.a: Yahweh said the city would become like Topheth.

questions.q: What were the people of Judah and Jerusalem doing on the rooftops of their houses?
questions.a: They were burning incense to the stars and pouring out drink offerings to other gods.

questions.q: Why will Yahweh bring disaster on the city and all of its towns?
questions.a: Yahweh will bring disaster on them because they stubbornly refused to listen to what he said to them.

commentary.text: By the type of breaking an earthen vessel, Jeremiah is to predict the destruction of Judah.

Jer. 19:1-9 The prophet must give notice of ruin coming upon Judah and Jerusalem. Both rulers and ruled must attend to it. That place which holiness made the joy of the whole earth, sin made the reproach and shame of the whole earth. There is no fleeing from God's justice, but by fleeing to his mercy.

Jer. 19:10-15 The potter's vessel, after it is hardened, can never be pieced again when it is broken. And as the bottle was broken, so shall Judah and Jerusalem be broken by the Chaldeans. No human hand can repair it; but if they return to the Lord he will heal. As they filled Tophet with the slain sacrificed to their idols, so will God fill the whole city with the slain that shall fall as sacrifices to his justice. Whatever men may think, God will appear as terrible against sin and sinners as the Scriptures state; nor shall the unbelief of men make his promise or his threatenings of no effect. The obstinacy of sinners in sinful ways, is their own fault; if they are deaf to the word of God, it is because they have stopped their ears. We have need to pray that God, by his grace, would deliver us from hardness of heart, and contempt of his word and commandments.
